subject: Learning Methods
title: Notes as Thinking Tools
description: A quick win: understand Notes as Thinking Tools.

hook.text: Richard Feynman said he didn't take notes to remember things. He took notes to think about things.

buildup.text: Writing externalizes thought. When ideas are on paper, you can see them, rearrange them, and spot gaps.

discovery.text: Working memory holds only a few items. Paper holds unlimited items. Offloading frees mental space for higher-order.

twist.text: The most valuable notes are not records of what someone else said. They are records of your own evolving thoughts.

climax.text: Use notes to develop ideas, not just store them. Write to think, not just to remember.

punchline.text: Notes are for thinking, not just recording.

quiz.question: According to Feynman's approach, what is the primary purpose of note-taking?
options: To create a permanent archive of lectures
To think about and develop ideas on paper
